title: Cross-squad Commitment Ledger and Lifecycle Badging
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Roadmap handoffs across Eng/Design/Security/Infra lack a single source of truth for commitments and lifecycle state. Teams are tracking dependencies in spreadsheets, ad-hoc Linear links, and meeting notes which leads to missed cross-team signals during rollouts (late security reviews, unscoped infra changes, design signoff delays).

Goal: Create a lightweight, operational "Commitment Ledger" that surfaces every cross-squad dependency, its current lifecycle badge (Proposed / Committed / In Flight / At Risk / Blocked / Resolved), explicit owners, target release window, and required gates (e.g., security review, infra capacity). The ledger will be integrated into Linear and the Console roadmap view and emit weekly cadence summaries to squad leads.

Scope: Minimum viable ledger for Q2 launches: schema, Linear issue template, Console dependency strip, automated weekly digest, and an escalation pattern for At Risk -> Canary -> Executive review. This ticket covers PM-side design of the ledger, acceptance criteria, alignment workshops, and pilot with two squads (Model Serving and Console). Engineering ownership and design assets are tracked as dependencies.

Out-of-scope: Full automated enforcement (blocking PR merges) and org-wide migration of historical dependencies (to be considered in follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Commitment ledger schema documented in Confluence with examples (link below)
Linear issue template created and linked to project board; new cross-squad issues created using template in pilot squads
Lifecycle badging (6 states) implemented visually in Console roadmap strip for pilot squads
Weekly digest email and Slack summary for squad leads, seeded from ledger data
Escalation runbook (At Risk -> Canary -> Exec) published and verified in tabletop exercise

risks: Auditability: initial ledger is a cached view (sync from Linear) - risk of drift if teams don't update issues
Security gating adds lead time; without clear SLOs teams may mark things Committed prematurely
Engineering bandwidth: ENG-9182 spike shows integration work may slip if infra priority changes
Adoption risk: squads may prefer existing ad-hoc processes unless incentives and low friction integrations are provided
